overloadMerges.note: Autoparse's return-type regex only recognizes ': Type' at the end of a signature; this doc uses the legacy '-> Integer' arrow form, so the top-level '(...)' match failed and the draft overload has zero params/no returns. Reconstructed the full param list from the parameter table and prose for this syntax (optional start/lengthFound pair plus optional trailing '*').

params.name: start
params.description: Position in string where the search will start; defaults to the first character.

params.name: lengthFound
params.description: Length of the string actually found by the search.
If passed, evaluation is based on character codes (letters written with one or more characters, e.g. æ/ae, are not treated as equivalent).

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Returns the position of the first occurrence of find in aString using 4D's default global/linguistic comparison, optionally restricted to a strict character-code comparison via '*'.

discriminatedBy.rule: This is the general-purpose overload (default global comparison, optional strict '*' mode); the other overload replaces '*' with a mandatory options parameter for finer-grained search condition control and requires start/lengthFound to be passed explicitly.

overloadMerges.note: Same regex failure as overload 0 (this doc line also ends in '-> Integer'); reconstructed the full mandatory param list from the parameter table and prose for the options-based syntax.

params.name: start
params.description: Position in string where the search will start.

params.name: lengthFound
params.description: Length of the string actually found by the search.

params.name: options
params.description: Search condition(s), combinable constants replacing the simpler '*' toggle of the other overload.

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Returns the position of the first occurrence of find in aString using an explicit, combinable set of search-condition constants (options) instead of the simple '*' character-code toggle.

discriminatedBy.rule: Selected when finer control over comparison rules is needed than the plain overload's '*' flag provides; start and lengthFound are mandatory in this form.

constraints: Returns 0 if aString does not contain find, including when both are empty strings.
By default, comparisons are global/linguistic (e.g. æ = ae) but not diacritical (a ≠ à).
